item.title: ‘Princess of Wales’ returns: Kate Middleton calls on businesses to put people first in her first speech in two years
item.description: Princess Kate Middleton made her first public speech in two years. She spoke at the Future Workforce Summit in London. Her focus was on early childhood development. She urged business leaders to support families and caregiving. This marks her return to royal duties after cancer treatment. Her appearance signals a continuation of her important campaign.

item.description: Streamer xQc alleges QTCinderella nominated Vanillamace for an award to mend past issues. This has sparked debate about fairness in creator awards. The situation highlights ongoing discussions about transparency in online award shows.

item.title: Adin Ross to take legal action after Cuffem suffers major head injury at Carti concert
item.description: Streamer Adin Ross is preparing legal action after his friend Cuffem sustained a severe head injury when a platform railing collapsed at a Playboi Carti concert. Ross alleges the venue's negligence caused the "completely preventable" accident, leading to Cuffem's hospitalization and surgery. Ross vows to hold the venue accountable for its safety failures.

item.description: “There could be a little bit of, almost, quiet time in the labor market, because firms are finding that AI is making their workers so productive that they don’t necessarily have to hire the new kids out of college and so on," Hassett said, assuring that AI-induced softness in the market would be temporary.

item.title: After a 3-year ban, SteveWillDoIt is finally back — Here’s what we know so far
item.description: Popular YouTuber SteveWillDoIt is making a highly anticipated return to the platform after a three-year ban for gambling promotions. He announced his comeback for December 24th, promising a million-dollar giveaway upon reaching one million subscribers. This marks a new, ambitious chapter for the creator, aiming for a grander scale with a TV show-like experience.

item.title: NASA astronaut’s estranged partner pleads guilty over false ‘space crime’ allegation
item.description: A six-year 'space crime' saga concludes as Summer Worden admits to falsely accusing astronaut Anne McClain of accessing her bank account from the ISS. Worden pleaded guilty to making false statements to investigators, ending years of speculation. McClain, cleared of any wrongdoing, continues her distinguished NASA career.

item.title: Trump rolls out red carpet for MBS as US takes to green flags
item.description: Donald Trump welcomed Saudi Prince Mohammed bin Salman with a red carpet and military honors, signaling a strategic reset in U.S. regional relations. The visit secured billions in business deals, including arms sales and nuclear cooperation, despite ongoing criticism over the Khashoggi murder. This recalibration also impacts U.S. ties with Pakistan and India.

item.title: Americans never asked for it: Missouri senator calls for termination of OPT, says it's 'cheap labor pipeline'
item.description: "OPT serves the financial interests of large corporations and academic institutions at the direct expense of young American workers and students. This system boxes young Americans out of the workforce, discriminates against American workers in favour of foreign labor, suppresses wages and job opportunities for US graduates," Senator Eric Schmitt wrote.

item.title: F-35 fighter jets, AI, hotels: Donald Trump to meet Saudi Arabia’s crown prince - what’s at stake
item.description: President Donald Trump hosts Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman in Washington. Discussions focus on a significant F-35 fighter jet sale. Saudi Arabia plans substantial investments in US artificial intelligence and data centers. The visit also brings attention to the Trump family's business dealings with Saudi entities. The shadow of Jamal Khashoggi's killing also looms over the high-profile engagement.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: How Pluto captured a moon almost its own size
item.description: Pluto's largest moon, Charon, likely formed through a capture event in the early, crowded Kuiper Belt. Three-body encounters and tidal forces allowed Charon to lose energy and become permanently bound, leading to the system's unique binary-like configuration and high angular momentum. This process offers insights into the formation of distant worlds.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: West Bank terror incident: At least 1 killed, multiple injured in ramming-stabbing at Gush Etzion; suspects ‘neutralised’
item.description: A combined vehicle-ramming and stabbing attack at the Gush Etzion Junction in the West Bank resulted in one death and three injuries. Three suspected attackers were neutralized by Israeli forces, who also found explosives in the assailants' vehicle. The incident occurred amidst escalating settler violence in the region.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Divorce to donations: Jeff Bezos’s ex-wife MacKenzie Scott donates $700 million to historically black colleges in another philanthropic move
item.description: Philanthropist MacKenzie Scott has gifted over 700 million dollars to several historically black colleges and universities. This significant contribution aims to bolster institutions that have historically faced underfunding. The donations are unrestricted, allowing schools to invest in academics, scholarships, and facilities. This move highlights Scott's commitment to addressing economic inequality and racial injustice through her substantial wealth.

item.title: ‘Until they learn...’: Trump’s new clarification on H-1B confuses Americans; ‘We aren’t buying it’
item.description: Trump defended his earlier statement that America needs certain talents and added 'until they learn' for clarification amid a raging H-1B controversy. “For instance, if you’re going to be making chips, we don’t make chips too much here anymore,” he said. “But we have to train our people how to make chips because we didn’t do it. We used to do it and then, foolishly, we lost that business to Taiwan," he said.
